title: Nanosight LM10 Cleaning Protocol
author: Joshua A Welsh
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.be58jg9w
materials: Open up the most recent version of the NanoSight software (3.4 as of January 2020)
Turn the camera on inside the NTA software by clicking "Start camera"
Current temperature: Measure using thermometer on table
At the end of the 3 captures, allow the software to automatically analyze the data
If you need to measure another sample:
Turn the camera on inside the NTA software by clicking "Start camera"
To adjust settings, press: SOP - 1. Standard Measurement 2. Number of Captures: 3 3. Capture Duration(s): 30 4. Current temperature: Measure using thermometer on table

steps.title: System Power-Up
steps.instruction: Initialize the hardware and computer systems.

substeps.instruction: Turn on the black power strip.
Turn on the computer on the shelf and login using the password written above the screen.
Turn on the Nanosight microscope (confirm the camera fan turns on).

steps.title: Inspect and Clean Module Optics
steps.instruction: Remove the storage lens paper from between the stainless steel cover and the optical flat of the LM10 module, then inspect for smudges or particles.

substeps.instruction: Examine the translucent window of the steel cover; blow off external dust/lint using compressed air.

Clean the inside of the window by dipping a folded piece of lens paper into 1% MICRO 90 (poured into a 50 mL conical cap), gently cleaning the surface. Repeat this process using a new piece of lens paper dipped in DPBS, then dry with lens paper.

Clean the optical flat by dipping a folded piece of lens paper into 1% MICRO 90 (poured into a 50 mL conical cap). Wipe the optical flat, focusing on the translucent rectangle, pressing firmly perpendicularly and parallel to the edge (do not wipe in circles).

steps.title: Reassemble Module
steps.instruction: Quickly place the steel cover back onto the module and screw it in, tightening screws in a diagonal pattern without over-tightening.

steps.title: Initial DPBS Flush
steps.instruction: Flush the LM10 module to remove contaminants and air bubbles using DPBS.

substeps.instruction: Load 10 mL of DPBS into a 12 mL syringe.
Insert the syringe into the white plastic entry port (the only port on its side) while holding the module as vertically as possible. Slowly inject DPBS to avoid bubbles on the viewing window.
Once liquid fills the fluid exit port, flip the module so the syringe is standing straight up and slowly press the plunger until all DPBS passes into a waste container.
If bubbles form, push the fluid all the way through; do not reverse the syringe.
Return the module to its original vertical position and slowly draw out remaining DPBS from the viewing window.
Discard the used DPBS in a waste container.

steps.title: Secondary DPBS Flush
steps.instruction: Perform a secondary flush to ensure the system is clear.

substeps.instruction: Draw 6 mL of DPBS into the syringe. If bubbles were present in the initial flush, push the entire volume through and add another 6 mL.
Flush the NanoSight with ~5 mL of DPBS, leaving less than 1 mL in the syringe.

steps.title: Microscope Setup and Alignment
steps.instruction: Install the module and align the viewing window.

substeps.instruction: Slide the LM10 module into the grooved slot on the microscope table.
Ensure the 20X lens is in use.
Plug the power source into the side of the LM10 module and flip the silver switch on the right side to turn on the laser.
Use focusing knobs/stage mover to locate the 'thumb-print' (a large purple oval) and center it in the window.

Move the screen to the right until a large vertical line appears. Position the viewing frame immediately to the right of this line (the line should not be in the window). If the line is not vertical, slightly rotate the camera module.

steps.title: Final Particle Check
steps.instruction: Verify the NanoSight is clear of particles or noise before sample loading.

substeps.instruction: Check for remaining particles. If present, turn off the laser, disconnect power, and repeat the flushing process with a new aliquot of PBS and a new syringe.
If large fluorescent smudges or significant white background noise are present, turn off the laser, disconnect power, and repeat the cleaning of the optical flat/window and flushing (steps 6-15).
If clear, turn off the laser and slowly pull the remaining PBS out with the syringe.

steps.title: Sample Preparation and Loading
steps.instruction: Prepare and load the sample into the module.

substeps.instruction: Dilute samples as needed in a 2 mL low protein-binding Eppendorf tube and vortex thoroughly.
Draw the sample into a 1 mL syringe, pulling the plunger down to remove bubbles.
Load the sample into the LM10 module through the fluid entry port.
Turn on the laser.

steps.title: Sample Focusing and Optimization
steps.instruction: Adjust the viewing window and verify sample concentration.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the NanoSight is in the correct viewing window and properly focused.
Verify concentration: it is too dilute if <10 particles are on screen; it is too concentrated if there is significant fluorescent background or particles cannot be distinguished.

steps.title: Data Acquisition
steps.instruction: Record the sample using the software script.

substeps.instruction: Press 'Create and run script,' enter sample name and dilution, and hit 'OK'.
When the fan turns off, the instrument is recording. Ensure the table is not bumped or vibrated and do not lean over the table.
After each 30-second capture, press 'OK' and carefully press the plunger until particles on the screen move.
Turn the laser off as soon as data analysis begins.
Once analysis is complete, hit 'Export'.

steps.title: Post-Run Cleaning
steps.instruction: Flush the device and perform a deep clean of the module.

substeps.instruction: Flush the device with at least 2x12 mL syringes of DPBS.
Check the viewing frame for particles or smudges. If particles remain, repeat the full opening and cleaning process.
Perform a final deep clean: Open the module and wipe the optical flat with 1% MICRO 90, then wipe with lens paper wetted with pure water, and finally dry with a dry piece of lens paper.

Wipe all components that contacted DPBS (including sides, corners, and edges) with a Kimwipe or lens paper wetted with pure water, then dry with compressed air. Do not pour or pipette water directly onto the module.
Place a piece of folded, dry lens paper between the optical flat and steel cover plate.
Turn off all power sources.

steps.title: Data Transfer
steps.instruction: Transfer recorded files to a flash drive following the path: This PC -> J'D (H:) -> Nanosight files -> Nanovideos -> Date of recording.
